title: Refugee camps in sub-Saharan Africa
caption: A point on this map can represent decades of displacement. I mapped camp sites recorded between 1999 and 2024, with circle size showing years in operation and colour distinguishing sites open or closed at the end of 2024.

title: The routes that connect the world
caption: The oceans look open, but shipping follows remarkably concentrated paths. Brighter lines show denser traffic; the closer view brings the Red Sea, Gulf of Aden and Strait of Hormuz into focus.
source: World Bank and IMF, Global Shipping Traffic Density

title: What Africa exports
caption: One leading export gives each country its colour. This map compares the highest-value HS four-digit export products in 2024, excluding aircraft and ships. It is a view of leading products, not the whole export basket.

title: Where submarine cables come ashore
caption: The internet has a coastal geography. I used DBSCAN to group nearby cable landing points. Colours show the number of landing points in each cluster; grey points fall outside the clusters. The source includes existing and planned infrastructure at approximate locations.

title: How clear is the ocean?
caption: A view of the ocean through the light it absorbs and scatters. Lower Kd490 values mean light penetrates farther into the water. These satellite estimates show light attenuation, not a direct measure of water quality.
source: ESA Ocean Colour CCI v6.0 via NOAA OceanWatch (monthly, September 2026)

title: The age of the world’s temperature records
caption: Some weather stations give us a much longer view of the past than others. The colours mark when each station’s temperature record begins, set in a double-hemisphere layout inspired by older atlases. An early start does not necessarily mean an uninterrupted record.

title: Where land lies opposite land
caption: What lies on the other side of the Earth? I overlaid land with its antipodes. Orange marks places where land has land directly opposite it, pairing distant regions on the same globe.

title: The wind that could power Somalia
caption: A different way to look at Somalia’s landscape: through its wind. The colours show modelled mean wind speed at 100 metres above ground. They help reveal the resource, but do not tell us where a wind farm would be feasible or how much electricity it would produce.
source: Global Wind Atlas 3; AWS Terrain Tiles; Natural Earth

title: Where people live in Türkiye
caption: Population has a geography that administrative borders can hide. This map shows gridded population across Türkiye, with a closer view of İstanbul. The raised, brighter areas represent greater population in the mapped cells, not terrain elevation.
source: European Commission, Global Human Settlement Layer (2025 population estimates)

title: Where Africa is splitting apart
caption: A continent viewed through its relief and plate boundaries. The East African Rift and the Red Sea stand out against the surrounding landscape. Elevation and bathymetry provide the setting; the marked boundaries come from a tectonic plate model.
source: NOAA ETOPO 2022; PB2002 plate boundaries (Bird, 2003); Natural Earth

title: New York City: nighttime noise reports
caption: Where does New York report noise after dark? I grouped NYC 311 noise reports from July 2025, between 11 pm and 7 am, into hexagons. Purple marks fewer reports; pink, orange and yellow mark more. These are complaints, not measured sound levels.
source: NYC 311 Service Requests, NYC Open Data (July 2025)

title: Global markets after the tariff announcement
caption: How did selected stock markets move around the April 2025 tariff announcement? This animation follows local closing index levels relative to 2 April. Coral marks a fall and teal a rise. The timeline is descriptive: it does not isolate the effect of tariffs from everything else happening in markets.
source: Yahoo Finance daily index closes, 26 March–24 April 2025

title: The Red Sea shift
caption: Watch traffic thin through the Red Sea while crossings around the Cape increase. Red and orange show declines from the November baseline, blue little change, and turquoise and lime increases. The routes are illustrative; the changing counts come from PortWatch observations.
source: IMF PortWatch / UN Global Platform (daily vessel crossings)
